title: AI Assistant Competition Shifts Toward Work Context Management: Tencent WorkBuddy Restructures Task Organization with Grouping and Multi-Folder Associations

content_html:
On November 19, Tencent WorkBuddy released a task management upgrade for desktop version 5.11.3 and later. The original "Tasks" has been renamed "Recent," and "Spaces" has been upgraded to "Groups." The left sidebar has changed from a time-ordered task list to a work directory organized by work items.

Users can create groups through the group selector below the new-task input box, the entry to the right of the "Groups" heading in the sidebar, or the entry to the right of a task item. Drag and drop to categorize; while dragging, the task name is shown and the target group is highlighted. Users can also categorize or ungroup tasks through the group menu under the "···" on the right side of a task. Grouped tasks are still shown in "Recent" by default. In their "···" menu, users can select "Hide tasks from other sections" to avoid duplicate distractions.

Sorting and pinning are now customizable as well. Groups are sorted by update time by default. After switching to manual sorting, users can drag to adjust them. The "Recent" and "Groups" sections can also swap positions. Both tasks and groups can be pinned to the "Pinned" area at the top of the left sidebar. This area also supports drag-and-drop sorting, making it easy in multitasking scenarios to separate groups by project and place frequently used content within easy reach.

File association is another key feature. Previously, a group could be linked to only one local folder, and searching across folders incurred extra token consumption. In the new version, when creating or editing a group, users can use "Link folders on your computer" to select multiple folders at once. A single group can be linked to up to 16 local folders, and users can designate a "Primary" folder for WorkBuddy to prioritize. The first linked folder is set as Primary by default, and users can hover to switch it later. Removing a link only removes the association; it does not delete local files.

This update integrates task organization and local file context into the same grouping dimension, continuing the product direction of the AI office assistant evolving from a chat tool into a sustainable workspace.
